evidence.title: Esther Hasson
evidence.text: Esther Voorhees Hasson was the first Superintendent of the United States Navy Nurse Corps.

evidence.title: Esther Hasson
evidence.text: Prior to and after serving in the United States Navy Nurse Corps, she served as an Army nurse.

evidence.title: Navy Nurse
evidence.text: Navy Nurse is a 1945 American short film directed by D. Ross Lederman and starring Warren Douglas, Andrea King, and Marjorie Riordan.

evidence.title: Elizabeth Leonhardt
evidence.text: Elizabeth Leonhardt( 1867- 1953) was one of the Sacred Twenty, the first 20 nurses in the United States Navy Nurse Corps during World War I.

evidence.title: Elizabeth Leonhardt
evidence.text: She was the Chief Nurse of the US Navy Nurse Corps in 1919.

evidence.title: Ruth Alice Erickson
evidence.text: Captain Ruth Alice Erickson was the Director of the United States Navy Nurse Corps, serving in that position from 1962 to 1966.

evidence.title: Ruth Alice Erickson
evidence.text: As a lieutenant in the Navy Nurse Corps, she witnessed the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii on 7 December 1941.

evidence.title: Mariann Stratton
evidence.text: Rear Admiral Mariann Stratton( born 1945) was the Director of the United States Navy Nurse Corps from 1991 to 1994.

evidence.title: D. Ross Lederman
evidence.text: David Ross Lederman (December 12, 1894 – August 24, 1972) was an American film director noted for his Western/action/adventure films of the 1930s and 1940s.

evidence.title: D. Ross Lederman
evidence.text: Starting out as an extra in Mack Sennett's Keystone Cops series, Lederman worked his way through the ranks of film production, and first made his mark as a second-unit director.

evidence.title: D. Ross Lederman
evidence.text: He directed several B-Western serials in the early 1930s, such as "Two-Fisted Law" and "Texas Cyclone" both 1932, in which he worked with Tim McCoy and a young John Wayne.

evidence.title: D. Ross Lederman
evidence.text: Becoming a full feature director in the late 1930s, Lederman specialized in action films and especially westerns, continuing to produce films with McCoy at Columbia Pictures.

evidence.title: The Face in the Fog
evidence.text: The Face in the Fog is a 1922 American silent film produced by Cosmopolitan Productions and distributed by Paramount Pictures.

evidence.title: The Face in the Fog
evidence.text: It was directed by Alan Crosland and starred Lionel Barrymore.

evidence.title: The Face in the Fog
evidence.text: An incomplete print is preserved at the Library of Congress.

evidence.title: Alan Crosland
evidence.text: Alan Crosland (August 10, 1894 – July 16, 1936) was an American stage actor and film director.

evidence.title: Alan Crosland
evidence.text: He is noted for having directed the first film using spoken dialogue, "The Jazz Singer".

evidence.title: A Face in the Fog
evidence.text: A Face in the Fog is a 1936 American film directed by Robert F. Hill.

evidence.title: Myn M. Hoffman
evidence.text: Myn M. Hoffman was the fourth Superintendent of the United States Navy Nurse Corps.
